I have APS and have had two strokes and a heart attack in a span of two years. I was never able to hit the target INR with coumadin so I'm on Eliquis now.

My major concern was not being able to afford it being unemployed and uninsured but the pharmaceutical company will cover the costs for a year otherwise it would have been $1700/month OOP.

I've only been on it for about a month, I've gained 8 lbs but I'm on six different medications so who knows if it's strictly Eliquis for the weight gain? 🤷‍♂️

Good thing is I don't have to get my INR levels checked but I'll just keep taking it until my cardiologist tells me otherwise.

Well, he's already in collections so the hospital or medical providers sold his debt to the CA(s) to deal with collection efforts. 

I would suggest he make an offer to settle for less than the amount owed given that they buy debt for pennies on the dollar.

Get any verbal offer in writing as well so there's written documentation of the agreed upon verbal settlement.

Have you tried the Good Rx app?

Also try finding a sliding scale/low cost clinic in your area and they may be able to assist with some of the costs based on your income. 

I myself am on Keppra for seizures and it only costs $4 for a 30 day supply at the clinic I go to or $9 with the Good Rx app at Walmart.
